proposal: Replace the SPY-only momentum sleeve with index rotation: each month hold the top 1-2 of SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, EFA, EEM by 12-month return (only if positive, else cash).
rationale: Compare other major indices instead of only SPY; capture leadership shifts (e.g. emerging markets, small caps).
author: you
evidence: Backtested 2004-2026 in research/INDEX_ROTATION.md: same Sharpe (0.60 vs 0.58) at higher volatility, walk-forward 8.3%/yr (Sharpe 0.45) vs live 10.2% (0.61), desk Sharpe 0.86 vs 0.89. Claude recommends reject; awaiting your decision.

proposal: Rotate into the best-performing indices and avoid the worst: hold all but the 1-2 weakest of SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, EFA, EEM (positive momentum only), optionally rank-weighted toward the leaders.
rationale: Follow index leadership while staying diversified; avoid laggards rather than betting on one winner.
author: you
evidence: Backtested 2004-2026 (research/INDEX_ROTATION.md, follow-up): Sharpe 0.54-0.58 vs live 0.58, fragile to lookback and to removing QQQ, walk-forward 8.0%/yr (0.44) vs 10.2% (0.61), desk Sharpe 0.84-0.85 vs 0.89. Claude recommends reject; awaiting your decision.

proposal: Replace the bottleneck sleeve's engine with plain stock momentum: the 20 large companies with the best 6-month return (skipping the latest week), above their 40-week average, re-picked every 4 weeks; optionally keep the 100-day sell rule between re-picks.
rationale: Weekly-strategy experiment (research/WEEKLY.md) found 6-12 month momentum beat the average stock in 11 of 13 years; it is simpler and better tested than the flow rotation.
author: claude
evidence: Owner chose option 2 on 2026-10-20: plain momentum (top 20 by 6-month return, above the 200-day average, re-picked every 4 weeks) WITH the 100-day sell rule between re-picks. Backtest: sleeve 19.8%/yr, Sharpe 0.76, worst drop -30%; desk Sharpe 0.92 vs 0.88. Goes live at the bottleneck sleeve's 2026-11-03 re-pick (methods.DESK_SWITCH) so current picks aren't sold early.

proposal: Add an account-level circuit breaker to the desk: after a 2% day, 5% week or 8% month loss, block new buys (sells still go through) until the next weekday / Monday / first of next month.
rationale: From the drawdown-circuit-breaker skill in tradermonty/claude-trading-skills, reviewed 2026-10-21 at the user's request.
author: claude
evidence: Rejected by the user 2026-10-21. Backtest 2014-2026 (research/CIRCUIT_BREAKER.md): freeze 15.9%/yr, Sharpe 0.79 vs 16.4%, 0.81 without; go-to-cash 11.1%, 0.61; worst drop unchanged (~-33%).

proposal: Run the overnight drift strategy as a separate paper experiment in its own Alpaca paper account: each month lock the 20 large US stocks with the highest 12-month average overnight return; buy them market-on-close every trading day and sell everything market-on-open; log every fill against the official close/open to measure the auction cost.
rationale: research/OVERNIGHT.md: persistent (t 6.4, 82% of months), 15.5%/yr at 0.02% costs, break-even ~0.045% per trade. The open question is the real cost.
author: you
evidence: Accepted by the user 2026-10-21 ('build it'), as a paper experiment in its own account, separate from the desk. Paper fills are simulated: this tests the mechanics, not real auction costs. Superseded by 330e76e0: the sleeve runs inside the desk's account instead of a separate one.

rationale: Owner's request 2026-10-21: 'change the SPY momentum sleeve for the overnight trade - high conviction desk'.

proposal: Entry filter: a stock must also be above its 100-day average to be picked (not only its 200-day), so the 100-day sell rule can't fire on the pick day; the next-ranked stocks fill the slots.
rationale: Owner's question 2026-10-21: 5 of 20 picks would be sold straight away (whipsaw).
author: you
evidence: Backtest 2014-2026 (research/MOMENTUM_ENTRY.md): entry filter 19.4%/yr, Sharpe 0.75, 92% invested vs live behaviour (sold on the pick day) 17.9%, 0.71, 86%; beat it in 8 of 13 years. Accepted by the owner 2026-10-21, from that evening's first pick.

proposal: Hold the momentum sleeve's top 10 instead of top 20 (2% of the desk each instead of 1%), keeping the live rules: above the 200 and 100-day averages to be picked, re-picked every 28 days, sold below the 100-day average. Switch at the next re-pick (2026-11-18) if accepted.
rationale: research/DESK_TOP10.md: desk Sharpe 1.06 vs 0.98 (overnight at 0.02%), +2.2%/yr, better in both halves and 11 of 13 years, holds at 3x momentum costs, worst drop unchanged (-25.6% vs -25.9%). Caveats: survivors-only prices flatter concentration; '10' was chosen after an earlier test; single-stock risk doubles.
author: you
evidence: Backtested: research/desk_top10.py -> research/DESK_TOP10.md (2014-2026 monthly, survivors-only). Desk Sharpe 1.06 vs 0.98, 90% bootstrap range of the gap +0.02 to +0.12; return gap t 3.0. Awaiting the owner's decision.

proposal: Buy with ordinary market orders in the last minutes before the close (3:55-3:59pm New York) instead of market-on-close orders. Same picks, sizing and next-open sale.
rationale: 2026-10-21, the first night: Alpaca's paper account filled the closing-auction orders only in part - 5 of 20 in full, 5 partly, 10 not at all (expired) - so about $8,600 was invested instead of $30,000. Paper market orders fill in full; prices 1-5 minutes before the close are close to what the research assumed. Paper fills still can't measure real costs.
author: you
evidence: Owner chose 'Market orders at 3:57pm' on 2026-10-22 after the partial auction fills. Implemented as a 3:55-3:59pm window; the scheduled buy now fires at 3:54pm.

proposal: Regime checks: no overnight buys (cash for the night) when SPY is below its 200-day average, or on a day tech stocks lag defensive stocks by more than on 90% of past days (SIC groups in ai_desk/overnight_groups.json). Checked at the 3:55pm buy from prices up to then; the cut-off is refreshed by each evening run from 5 years of daily closes.
rationale: research/OVERNIGHT_REGIME.md: 2014-2026, cash on either signal (25% of nights) gave Sharpe 1.03 vs 0.70, worst drop -16% vs -36%, both halves (1.00 / 1.13). Switching into defensive or low-beta stocks instead does not help. Caveats: ~20 rules tested; survivors-only prices; part of the gain is trading less; the tech signal only works same-day, so live it is judged at 3:55pm, a few minutes before the close the backtest used; live cut-off from a 5-year window vs the backtest's expanding one.
author: you
evidence: Backtested in research/overnight_regime.py. Owner: 'Add in the checks to the overnight sleeve' (2026-10-23) after reading the results.

proposal: Replace the regime check's tech-vs-defensive test with one on tonight's own picks: cash for the night when the 20 picks' average return from today's open to 3:55pm is -1.9% or worse (the research's worst 10% of days). The SPY 200-day rule stays.
rationale: research/overnight_picks_check.py (OVERNIGHT_REGIME.md follow-up): with the SPY rule, Sharpe 1.31 vs 1.03 for the tech-vs-defensive check, worst drop -17%, both halves (1.20 / 1.45); flagged nights -12.7 / -13.9 bp. Needs no industry lists (industries and the picks change). Caveats: the sixth variant on top of ~20 rules; judged at 3:55pm not the close; fixed cut-off from the backtest (stable -1.5% to -1.9% since 2015); survivors-only prices.

proposal: Rank by the plain 12-month return (adjusted closes) instead of the 12-month average overnight return, and re-pick every trading day instead of monthly: the evening run ranks on that day's close, the next afternoon's buy uses it. Picks-day cut-off -2.0% (this version's worst 10%). Watchlist cohort kept monthly.
rationale: research/lookbacks.py and research/overnight_v2.py (2014-2026, survivors-only): as it would run live (ranked the evening before) with the SPY and picks-day checks, Sharpe 1.54 vs 1.31, worst drop -15% vs -17%, better in both halves (1.43/1.71 vs 1.20/1.45) and 9 of 13 years; nightly gain +1.1 bp, t 1.1 - not significant. Daily re-picking costs nothing extra (all shares are sold each morning). Caveat: this ranks momentum stocks and holds them overnight - a different idea from the researched overnight effect; only 37% of nights' picks overlap with the old ranking.
author: you
evidence: Owner: 'Change overnight to add both small improvements' (2026-10-23).

proposal: Sell the overnight shares with market-on-open orders (the opening auction, which fills at the official open) instead of ordinary market orders at the open. Tested first as a live A/B test on paper: each evening, a fixed coin-flip half of the overnight-only holdings is left out of the evening run's orders and sold by a 9:05am market-on-open run; unfilled shares go out with the next evening's orders.
rationale: Live paper fills 2026-10-22 to 10-26: the overnight sales filled 0.45-0.68% below the official open each morning (49 sales), buys about 0.00% - about ten times the research's break-even of ~0.045% per trade, and roughly half of the sleeve's -$954 so far. Paper fills are simulated, so this tests the mechanics. Decision rule fixed in advance: after 10 trading days, adopt market-on-open for all overnight-only sales if its average cost vs the official open is at least 0.10 points lower than market orders' and at least 95% of its shares filled; otherwise keep market orders.
author: you
evidence: Rejected by the owner 2026-10-29: Alpaca paper does not fill market-on-open orders - all 20 sales (9 on 2026-10-28, 11 on 2026-10-29) expired unfilled, so the test could not reach its pre-set verdict (needs >= 95% filled) and the unfilled half was held through the day. From the 2026-10-29 evening run all overnight shares sell at the open with the desk's market orders; leftovers are still swept. Real auction prices stay tracked by the official-price line (6 nights: official -$527 vs paper -$1,384).

proposal: Add an RSI dip-buying overlay: when one of the 100 largest US companies (point-in-time) closes above its 200-day average with RSI(14) below 30, buy it at the next open and sell at the open after it first closes above its 5-day average (at most 10 days). Each position is 3% of the desk, at most 5 at once (15%), funded from the overnight sleeve's 30% while open (the overnight buys shrink by that much); the rest of the desk is unchanged. Sensitivity: a fixed 10% sleeve (5 slots of 2%) taken pro-rata from all sleeves, or from the quality screen.
rationale: research/CANDLE_RSI.md: candles added nothing, but this RSI rule made +1.0% a trade in 2014-19 and +1.2% in 2020-26 (t ~5 each; RSI 25/30/35 and 4x costs all positive; 11 of 13 years) with ~0.4 correlation to the market; survivors-only prices, and found after looking (not pre-registered). It is invested ~6% of the time, so it needs shared money rather than a fixed slice. Decision rule fixed before the desk test: recommend accepting only if the desk's Sharpe is higher in BOTH 2014-19 and 2020-26, the worst drop is no more than 1 point deeper, and the desk still beats the current one with the overlay at 0.20% costs each way; otherwise reject.
author: you
evidence: Owner: 'Propose the amendment and test it inside the desk' (2026-10-27). Desk backtest: research/desk_rsi.py -> research/DESK_RSI.md.

proposal: Rearrange the desk (research/DESK_5050.md, variant C): sell the quality screen (50%) and momentum (20%) sleeves, and run two sleeves in the same Alpaca paper account. (1) RSI dips: when one of the 100 largest US companies closes above its 200-day average with RSI(14) below 30, buy it at the next open as 10% of the desk; sell at the open after it first closes above its 5-day average, or after 10 trading days; at most 5 at once, same-day signals lowest RSI first. (2) Overnight: the existing sleeve and its rules, but it buys with all the cash the dips aren't using (less the 1% buffer) instead of 30% of equity - about 95% of the desk on an average night. Switch: the 2026-10-27 evening run sells quality and momentum at the 2026-10-28 open; the overnight sleeve's bigger buys start at the 2026-10-28 3:55pm window.
rationale: Backtest 2014-06 to 2026-09 (survivors-only prices): 28.1%/yr, Sharpe 1.78, worst drop -10.9% vs the current desk's 21.5%, 1.24, -21.0% - with the overnight sleeve at 0.02% costs each way. At 0.05% overnight costs: 15.2%/yr, Sharpe 0.99, worst -15.0% (0.22 in 2014-19). The result rests on the overnight sleeve's real trading costs, which aren't known yet: live paper sales at the open have filled 0.45-0.68% below the official open, and the market-on-open test (amendment e43f2959) is measuring it. Recommended against by Claude before the cost test reports; the owner chose to go live on paper now.
author: you
